items.example_en: I have a headache.
items.note: The hurting part is the subject: болит голова, болят ноги.

items.example_en: Give me your hand.
items.note: One word for hand and arm; нога likewise covers leg and foot.

items.example: У меня болят ноги после бега.
items.example_en: My legs hurt after running.
items.note: Plural ноги with a stress shift.

items.example_en: My back has hurt since yesterday.
The child has a stomach ache.
items.note: желудок is the organ; живот is the everyday word.

items.example_en: I have a sore throat.
I'm hungry, shall we eat something?
items.note: Literally I want to eat. There is no direct equivalent of to be hungry.

items.example_en: Are you thirsty? There's water in the fridge.
items.note: Literally I want to drink.

items.example_en: I'm cold, please close the window.
items.note: Dative plus an impersonal adverb. холодно alone means it is cold outside.

items.example_en: I feel sleepy, I'm going to lie down.
items.note: мне хочется is softer than я хочу: it just comes over you.

items.example_en: I need to rest.
items.note: Dative plus нужно plus infinitive. With a noun it agrees: мне нужна помощь.

items.example_en: Excuse me, where is the toilet?
items.note: Singular in Russian, unlike French.

items.example: С утра я плохо себя чувствую.
items.example_en: I haven't been feeling well since this morning.
items.note: чувствовать себя plus adverb: to feel a certain way. The в is silent.

items.example: У него температура уже два дня.
items.example_en: He's had a fever for two days.
items.note: температура alone implies a raised one.

items.example_en: The cough gets worse at night.
items.note: The verb is кашлять.

items.example_en: I think I've caught a cold.
items.note: Past tense agrees: простудился, простудилась.

items.example_en: It hurts here when I press.
items.note: An impersonal adverb again, not an adjective.

items.example: Как давно у вас эти боли?
items.example_en: How long have you had this pain?
I'd like to make an appointment with the doctor.
items.note: Literally to write oneself in. к plus dative: к врачу.

items.example_en: Here's the prescription, buy it at the pharmacy.
items.note: The same word as a cooking recipe.

items.example_en: This medicine is taken after meals.
items.note: The third-person plural without a subject expresses the passive.

items.example_en: You need to rest for three days.
items.note: Dative вам plus нужно plus perfective infinitive.

items.example_en: We called an ambulance last night.
items.note: Usually shortened to скорая. The emergency number in Russia is 112.

items.example_en: The health centre is open until eight.
items.note: The first stop for non-emergencies in the Russian system.

items.example: Я занимаюсь спортом три раза в неделю.
items.example_en: I exercise three times a week.
items.note: заниматься takes the instrumental: спортом, музыкой, языками.

items.example_en: I run along the canal.
items.note: бегать is habitual or multidirectional; бежать is one run in one direction.

items.example_en: I signed up at the gym.
items.note: Short for спортивный зал.

items.example_en: She's training for a marathon.
items.note: к plus dative for the goal you are training towards.

items.example: Ты отлично выглядишь, в хорошей форме!
items.example_en: You look great, in good shape!
My muscles ache everywhere today.
items.note: The muscles are the subject of болеть.

items.example_en: I slept badly last night.
items.note: этой ночью is instrumental, used adverbially for time.

items.english: to rest, to have a holiday
items.example_en: Rest, you need it.
items.note: Also means to be on holiday: мы отдыхали в Сочи.

items.example_en: Stress at work wears me out.
items.note: Borrowed straight from English.

items.example_en: At the weekend I try to relax.
items.note: Perfective расслабиться.

items.example_en: In winter you have to look after yourself.
Bye, take care!
items.note: A warm way to end a call or a message.
